title: Quantification of Saccharomyces cerevisiae pentose-phosphate pathway intermediates by LC-MS/MS
protocol: Inoculate 2 x 3 ml media with the yeast strain to be analyzed.
Shake or rotate overnight at 30 °C.
Use this overnight culture to adjust 2 x 30 ml yeast media to an OD600 of 0.1 - 0.2.
Grow the cells to mid-log phase, record OD600 value.
Centrifuge the 30 ml culture in a 50 ml tube for 3 min at 3000 g at room temperature.
Re-suspend the pellet in 1 ml HBSS buffer.
Transfer the suspension to a 1.5 ml screw tube.
Centrifuge for 30 sec at 5000g-7000g in a table-top centrifuge.
Remove the supernatant quickly.
Freeze the sample immediately in liquid nitrogen.
Place the tubes on dry ice and open them.
Add an equal volume of glass beads to the cell pellets.
Transfer the tubes to normal ice.
Add 800 μl of 98% HBSS / 2% perchloric acid.
Close the tubes.
Place them into the Fast-Prep-24 machine.
Start the machine at 6.5 m/s for 40 seconds.
Cool the tubes on ice for 5 minutes.
Repeat the fast-prep procedure.
Incubate the samples for 30 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge the samples for 2 minutes at greater than or equal to 14,000g and 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Freeze and store the samples at -80°C until LC-MS/MS analysis.
Aliquot the mid-log culture into 1.5 ml screw tubes.
Incubate the cultures in a thermo block for at least 5 minutes at 30°C.
Centrifuge at 5,000g to 7,000g for 30 seconds.
Remove the supernatant quickly.
Freeze the pellet immediately in liquid nitrogen.
Transfer the tubes to dry ice and open them.
Add an equal volume of glass beads to the cell pellet.
Place the tubes on normal ice.
Add 400 μl of 98% HBSS /2% perchloric acid.
Vortex for 4 minutes at maximum speed.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Vortex again for 4 minutes at maximum speed.
Incubate the samples for 30 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge the samples for 2 minutes at greater than or equal to 14,000g and 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Freeze and store the tubes at -80°C until LC-MS/MS analysis.
Thaw the samples for LC-MS/MS analysis.

Prepare calibrator curves for dihydroxacetone phosphate (dhap), ribose 5-phosphate (r5p), erythrose 4-phosphate (e4p), xylulose 5-phosphate or ribulose 5-phosphate (x5p), glucose 6-phosphate or fructose 6-phosphate (g6p), sedoheptulose 7-phosphate (s7p), and 6-phosphogluconate in the range of expected concentrations.
Add 50 μl of 10 μM 13C6-glucose-6-phosphate as an internal standard to 50 μl of lysates and calibrators.
Neutralize the samples with 1 M phosphate buffer (pH 11.5) to pH 7-8.
Centrifuge the samples for 5 min at greater than or equal to 14,000g, 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to appropriate HPLC vials.
Cap the HPLC vials securely.

Prepare the solvents for gradient-chromatography using 12.5% acetonitrile in water supplemented with 500 mg/l octylammonium acetate (pH 7.5) as binary solvent A and 50% acetonitrile in water supplemented with 500 mg/l octylammonium acetate (pH 7.5) as binary solvent B.
Equilibrate the C18 HPLC column with solvent A for several minutes at a flow rate of 1 ml/min.
Set a linear gradient from 100% solvent A to 40% solvent A and 60% solvent B in 8 min (at a flow rate of 1 ml/min).
If necessary, split the flow post-column dependent on your mass spectrometer.
Set the MS to multiple reaction monitoring mode (MRM) with the electrospray source operating in the negative-ion mode.

Configure your MS/MS to record the MRM transitions for dhap: m/z -169/-97; e4p: m/z -199/-97; r5p and x5p: m/z -229/-97; g6p: m/z -259/-97; <sup>13</sup>C<sub>6</sub>-glucose 6-P (IS): m/z -265/-97; 6pg: m/z -275/-97 and s7p: m/z -289/-97.
For relative quantification of the PPP intermediates, normalize the metabolites to the OD<sub>600</sub> value of the starter culture.
